answer: Each identity earns weight through a chained work ledger: every epoch, an agent must extend a randomly assigned parent answer with one verifiable improvement, sealed in a glacier no one can rewrite. A fresh clone starts at the canyon floor with no chain, unable to borrow another's history, since each link needs the graded output of the last. Clones multiply workload, not reward: a farm running a thousand chains pays a thousand times the effort, while one honest agent climbs one chain, keeping full weight. An oasis of shortcuts dries up fast — a copied link is caught and the chain voided.
